mainTopic: Horn signs that mark a חיה with permitted חלב, the כרכוז goat ruling, and the animals of בי עילאי with the קיסר stories
overview: The גמרא explains that the signs of a חיה are given so we know when its חלב is permitted: an animal with horns and split hooves. רבי דוסא adds that horns alone are enough, and that the one-horned קרש is permitted. The גמרא tests the horn sign against a goat, an ox and a צבי, and narrows it each time: the horns must be layered, grooved, branched, and then rounded. It concludes that branched horns are a sure sign of a חיה. Otherwise the horns must be layered, rounded and grooved, with grooves that blend together. This rule is behind the doubt about the כרכוז goat: רב אחאי forbade its fat and רב שמואל בריה דרבי אבהו ate it. ארץ ישראל ruled like רב שמואל, while warning people to honor רב אחאי. רב יהודה identifies the קרש as the gazelle of בי עילאי and the טגריס as the lion of בי עילאי, which leads to a story about the giant lion and the קיסר. A second story, in which the קיסר asks to see God, begins at the end and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why we need signs of a wild animal: to permit its fat
steps.stepSummary: The signs of a חיה are given so we know that its חלב is permitted. A kosher animal with horns and split hooves is a חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The signs are there to permit its fat. The ברייתא means: these are the signs of a חיה whose fat is permitted. Any animal that has horns and split hooves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering an earlier question: why do we need special signs for a חיה at all? The answer is that we need them to know when its חלב is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general kosher signs already tell us whether an animal may be eaten. These extra signs tell us something different: whether the animal is a חיה, because the חלב of a בהמה is forbidden and the חלב of a חיה is permitted. So the ברייתא is now read as a list of signs for a חיה with permitted fat.

keyTerms.meaning: Certain fats that are forbidden in a domestic animal but permitted in a wild animal
And this is what it means (the גמרא explains how to read the text)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole sugya. Every challenge that follows asks whether horns really prove that an animal is a חיה with permitted חלב.

phrases.english: To permit its fat,
and this is what it is saying:
These are the signs of a wild animal
whose fat is permitted:
any animal that has horns and split hooves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from before this section about why signs of a חיה are needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the purpose of the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Signs of a חיה seem unnecessary, since the general kosher signs already apply
steps.terutzMaskana: The signs tell us the animal is a חיה, so its חלב is permitted

steps.title: רבי דוסא: horns alone are enough, and a one-horned קרש is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא says that horns alone prove the animal is a חיה, but split hooves alone do not. A קרש with only one horn is also permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says: if it has horns, you do not need to check for split hooves. If it has split hooves, you still need to check for horns. And a קרש, even though it has only one horn, is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסא gives his own version of the signs. For him, horns are the main sign, and he adds a special case, the one-horned קרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every animal with horns also has split hooves, so finding horns is enough. Many animals with split hooves have no horns, so hooves alone prove nothing. The קרש is an exception: it has one horn instead of two, and it still counts as permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: To go back and check for, to look for
A kind of animal with a single horn

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says:
If it has horns,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה צָרִיךְ לַחֲזוֹר עַל טְלָפַיִם,
phrases.english: you do not need to check for split hooves;
if it has split hooves,
you do need to check for horns.

phrases.aramaic: וְקֶרֶשׁ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ
phrases.english: And a keresh, even though it has
only one horn, is permitted.
phrases.notes: He means its fat is permitted, like any other wild animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with רבי דוסא's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Horns alone are a sufficient sign of a חיה, hooves alone are not, and a one-horned קרש is permitted

steps.title: Challenge: a goat has horns and hooves, but its fat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether horns and hooves can really be the rule, since a goat has both and its חלב is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this a fixed rule? But a goat has horns and split hooves, and its fat is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the sign from the ברייתא by pointing to a goat, a domestic animal that has horns and split hooves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If horns and split hooves make an animal a חיה, then a goat should count as a חיה and its חלב should be permitted. But a goat is a בהמה and its חלב is forbidden, so the sign as stated is too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this a fixed rule? (a challenge to a general statement)
But look at (introduces a case that contradicts the rule)

phrases.english: Is this a fixed rule?

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי עֵז, דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ קַרְנַיִם וּטְלָפַיִם,
phrases.english: But there is the goat, which has horns and split hooves,
and its fat is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the sign given in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that horns and split hooves mark a חיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A goat has both signs, yet it is a בהמה with forbidden חלב

steps.title: Answer: the horns must be layered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the horns must be layered (כרוכות), and a goat's horns are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need layered horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rule by describing the horns more exactly. Not every horn counts, only layered horns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule stays, but it becomes narrower. A goat has horns, but not the layered kind, so it no longer breaks the rule.

phrases.english: We require layered horns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the goat challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any horns at all make the animal a חיה
steps.terutzMaskana: Only layered horns count, and a goat lacks them

steps.title: Challenge: an ox has layered horns, but its fat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new sign: an ox has layered horns, yet its חלב is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But an ox has layered horns, and its fat is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new sign, layered horns, against the ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox is a בהמה with forbidden חלב, but its horns are layered. So 'layered horns' still lets in a domestic animal.

phrases.english: But there is the ox, whose horns are layered,
and its fat is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ox has layered horns, yet it is a בהמה with forbidden חלב

steps.title: Answer: the horns must be grooved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the horns must be grooved (חרוקות), and an ox's horns are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need grooved horns.
steps.whatsHappening: Again the גמרא saves the rule by describing the horns more exactly, this time as grooved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grooved horns have ridges or notches along them. An ox's horns are smooth, so the ox no longer breaks the rule.

phrases.english: We require grooved horns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ox challenge
steps.terutzMaskana: The horns must be grooved, and an ox's are not

steps.title: Challenge: a goat has grooved horns, but its fat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The goat returns: its horns are grooved, yet its חלב is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a goat has grooved horns, and its fat is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the sign of grooved horns and finds that the goat breaks it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat was answered earlier because its horns are not layered. Now the sign being tested is grooved horns, and a goat's horns are grooved. So the goat breaks the rule again.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't be thrown by the goat coming back. Each new answer gives a different sign, and the גמרא checks that sign against every animal again, including ones it already handled.

phrases.english: But there is the goat, whose horns are grooved,
and its fat is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 6
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A goat has grooved horns, yet it is a בהמה with forbidden חלב

steps.title: Answer: the horns must be branched
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the horns must be branched (מפוצלות), and a goat's horns are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need branched horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the sign again: the horns must split into branches, like antlers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A goat's horns do not branch, so the goat no longer breaks the rule. But this sign is very narrow, and the next step tests it.

phrases.english: We require branched horns!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second goat challenge
steps.terutzMaskana: The horns must be branched, and a goat's are not

steps.title: Challenge: a gazelle's horns are not branched, but its fat is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges from the other direction: a צבי has no branched horns, yet its חלב is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a gazelle does not have branched horns, and its fat is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: This time the problem is that the sign is too narrow. It leaves out a real חיה, the צבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier challenges showed the sign let in domestic animals. Here the sign leaves out a true חיה, since a צבי's horns are not branched. So 'branched' cannot be a required sign.

keyTerms.meaning: Gazelle or deer, a classic חיה

phrases.english: But there is the gazelle, whose horns are not branched,
and its fat is permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 8 from the opposite side
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A צבי lacks branched horns, yet it is a חיה with permitted חלב, so the sign is too narrow

steps.title: Answer: the horns must be rounded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the horns must be rounded (חדורות), which also includes the צבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need rounded horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another description of the horns, round rather than flat, which fits the צבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of branched, the sign is now rounded horns. A צבי has rounded horns, so it counts as a חיה. The discussion of these horn signs continues after this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Rounded (horns that are round, not broad or flat)

steps.whatToRemember: The plain sign 'horns and split hooves' gets narrowed step by step: layered, grooved, branched, and then rounded. Each challenge is either a בהמה that slips in (goat, ox) or a חיה that gets left out (צבי).

phrases.english: We require rounded horns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the gazelle challenge
steps.terutzMaskana: Rounded horns are the sign, and the צבי has them

steps.title: The final rule for horn signs
steps.stepSummary: Branched horns settle the question: the animal is a חיה. Without branching, the horns must be layered, rounded and grooved, and the grooves must blend into each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore: if the horns are branched, there is no question at all. If they are not branched, they must be layered, rounded and grooved, and the grooves must run into one another.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the back-and-forth questions and answers, the גמרא gives its final summary of how horns show that an animal is a חיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Branching alone is enough, which covers animals like the deer. Without branching, all three signs are needed together (כרוכות, חדורות, חרוקות), which keeps out the goat (its horns are not layered) and the ox (its horns are not grooved). On top of that, the grooves must blend into each other.

keyTerms.meaning: 'neither judgment nor judge': there is no question at all
their grooves are absorbed, blending into one another

steps.whatToRemember: Branched horns mean a definite חיה. Unbranched horns need all three signs (layered, rounded, grooved), with grooves that blend together.

phrases.english: Therefore, where [the horns] are branched,
there is neither judgment nor judge;
phrases.notes: A saying that means there's nothing to discuss: it's surely a חיה, and its חלב is permitted.

phrases.english: where they are not branched,
we require layered, rounded, and grooved,
and that is provided their grooves are absorbed [into one another].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up all the horn signs worked out in the earlier steps of questions and answers.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Branched horns mean a חיה. Otherwise the horns must be layered, rounded and grooved, with grooves that blend together.

steps.title: The doubtful כרכוז goat in the house of the ריש גלותא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this rule is the source of the doubt about the עיזא כרכוז. It describes one such animal in the house of the ריש גלותא, from which a whole basket of fat was taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the doubt about the כרכוז goat. There was a כרכוז goat in the house of the ריש גלותא, and a full basket of fat was removed from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where the horn signs were unclear. This sets up the argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עיזא כרכוז looked like a goat, but its horns may have had the signs of a חיה. So it was unclear whether its fat counted as forbidden חלב. Because so much fat was involved (a full basket), the question mattered a lot.

keyTerms.meaning: a kind of goat-like animal whose status was in doubt
the Exilarch, head of the Jews in בבל
fat (the kind that is forbidden חלב in a בהמה)

phrases.english: And this is the doubt about the karkoz goat.
phrases.notes: 'This' means the horn rule from the last step. The doubt was whether its horns met those signs.

phrases.english: That certain karkoz goat
that was in the house of the Exilarch,
from which they removed a full basket of fat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the horn rule to a real case that was in doubt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The status of the עיזא כרכוז was in doubt because of the horn signs.

steps.title: רב אחאי forbids, רב שמואל eats
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי forbade the fat. רב שמואל בריה דרבי אבהו ate it, and he applied a פסוק to himself about being fed by the fruit of his own mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי said the fat was forbidden. רב שמואל son of רבי אבהו ate from it, and said about himself: 'A man's belly shall be filled with the fruit of his mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים disagree about the עיזא כרכוז. One treats it as a בהמה, and the other treats it as a חיה and eats the fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחאי held it was a בהמה, so its fat is forbidden חלב. רב שמואל held it was a חיה, so its fat is permitted. The פסוק he quoted means that his own Torah learning (the 'fruit of his mouth') is what let him know he could eat this food.

keyTerms.meaning: 'from the fruit of a man's mouth'

phrases.english: Rav Achai forbade [it],
Rav Shmuel son of Rabbi Abahu
ate from it,
he read about himself:
"A man's belly shall be filled with the fruit of his mouth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two opposite rulings on the case just described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אחאי forbids the fat of the עיזא כרכוז, while רב שמואל בריה דרבי אבהו permits it.

steps.title: The ruling from ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: A message came from ארץ ישראל: the הלכה follows רב שמואל, but be careful to honor רב אחאי, since he is a great light for the exile.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from there: The הלכה is like שמואל son of רבי אבהו, but be careful with the honor of our teacher אחאי, because he lights up the eyes of the exile.
steps.whatsHappening: The argument is settled: the הלכה is that the fat is permitted. But people must still show respect to רב אחאי, who forbade it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the case: the עיזא כרכוז is treated as a חיה, so its fat is permitted. The second half is about respect, not about the law itself. It tells people not to act against רב אחאי's ruling in a way that shames him.

keyTerms.meaning: they sent [a message] from there, from ארץ ישראל
be careful (here, careful about his honor)
lights up the eyes of the exile, a great teacher of the Jews in exile

steps.whatToRemember: The fat of the עיזא כרכוז is permitted, like רב שמואל. Even so, a great sage who disagrees must still be treated with honor.

phrases.english: They sent from there:

phrases.aramaic: הִלְכְתָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ,
phrases.english: The halacha is in accordance with Shmuel son of Rabbi Abahu,
but be careful with our teacher Achai,
phrases.notes: He means: be careful about his honor, so don't eat it in front of him.

phrases.english: for he lights up the eyes of the exile.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ מִתָּם: הִלְכְתָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument from the previous step.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב שמואל and the fat is permitted, but רב אחאי's honor must be kept.

steps.title: The קרש with one horn is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back a line from the ברייתא: the קרש has only one horn, yet its fat is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the קרש, even though it has only one horn, is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא it has been explaining and quotes its next case, the one-horned קרש. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The horn signs talk about horns in the plural, so you might think an animal with only one horn cannot qualify. The ברייתא teaches that the קרש is still a חיה, so its fat is permitted. It is an unusual case that still fits the category.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal with a single horn
permitted (here, its fat may be eaten)

phrases.aramaic: וְקֶרֶשׁ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ
phrases.english: And a keresh, even though it has
only one horn, is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקֶרֶשׁ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא קֶרֶן אַחַת, מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the כרכוז story and back to the ברייתא's list of cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קרש is a חיה even though it has only one horn, so its fat is permitted.

steps.title: רב יהודה identifies the קרש and the טגריס
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the קרש is the gazelle of בי עילאי, and the טגריס is the lion of בי עילאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The קרש is the gazelle of בי עילאי. The טגריס is the lion of בי עילאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which real animal the קרש is, and adds the name of another animal from the same place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a definition of terms: it tells us what the ברייתא's word קרש refers to. רב יהודה also identifies the טגריס while he is talking about animals of בי עילאי.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of a large wild animal
the name of a place (or forest)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
The keresh is the gazelle of Bei Ilai,
the tigris is the lion of Bei Ilai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: קֶרֶשׁ טַבְיָא דְּבֵי עִילַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the term קרש from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קרש is the gazelle of בי עילאי, and the טגריס is the lion of בי עילאי.

steps.title: The huge size of the animals of בי עילאי
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says the lion of בי עילאי measures nine אמות between its ears. רב יוסף says the gazelle of בי עילאי is sixteen אמות long.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: There are nine אמות between the ears of the lion of בי עילאי. רב יוסף said: The gazelle of בי עילאי is sixteen אמות long.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים add amazing facts about how huge the animals of בי עילאי are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These lines do not change the הלכה. They describe the giant size of the two animals רב יהודה just named, the lion and the gazelle.

keyTerms.meaning: cubits (אמות), a measure of about an arm's length

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: תְּשַׁע אַמְּהָתָא הָוֵי
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: There are nine cubits

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין אוּנָּא לְאוּנָּא דְּאַרְיָא דְּבֵי עִילַּאי.
phrases.english: between one ear and the other of the lion of Bei Ilai.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: שִׁיתְּסַר אַמְּהָתָא הָוֵי
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Sixteen cubits is
the length of the gazelle of Bei Ilai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: תְּשַׁע אַמְּהָתָא הָוֵי בֵּין אוּנָּא לְאוּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds descriptions of the lion and gazelle that רב יהודה just named.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lion of בי עילאי measures nine אמות between its ears, and its gazelle is sixteen אמות long.

steps.title: The emperor mocks the comparison of God to a lion
steps.stepSummary: The קיסר points out that God is compared to a lion in a פסוק in עמוס, and asks what is so great about that, since a horseman can kill a lion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The emperor said to רבי יהושע בן חנניה: Your God is compared to a lion, as the פסוק says, "A lion has roared, who will not fear?" What is so great about that? A horseman can kill a lion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story. The קיסר challenges the honor of God by attacking a פסוק that compares Him to a lion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument is simple: a comparison is only as impressive as the thing you compare to. Ordinary lions can be killed by a soldier on a horse, so comparing God to a lion seems to make Him small. This challenge sets up the answer, which ties back to the lion of בי עילאי from step 16.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ קֵיסָר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה:
phrases.english: The emperor said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya:
Your God is compared to a lion,
as it is written: "A lion has roared, who will not fear?"
What is His greatness?
A horseman can kill a lion!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ קֵיסָר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After describing the lion of בי עילאי, the גמרא brings a story that features it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of God to a lion in עמוס 3:8
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lion can be killed by a horseman, so comparing God to a lion seems to show weakness, not greatness.

steps.title: God is compared to the lion of בי עילאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן חנניה answers that the פסוק is not talking about an ordinary lion, but about the giant lion of בי עילאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He is not compared to this kind of lion. He is compared to the lion of בי עילאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן חנניה answers the קיסר. The lion in the פסוק is the giant lion of בי עילאי, not a normal one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer changes what the word "lion" refers to. The lion of בי עילאי is the enormous creature from steps 16 and 17, nine אמות between its ears, and no horseman could kill it. So the comparison does show greatness.

keyTerms.meaning: The lion of בי עילאי, the giant lion (טגריס) described earlier

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו כְּהַאי אַרְיָא מְתִיל,
phrases.english: He said to him: He is not compared to this kind of lion,
He is compared to the lion of Bei Ila'ei.
phrases.notes: This is the giant lion from earlier, the one רב כהנא said measures nine אמות between its ears.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קיסר's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the subject: the lion in the פסוק is a special, giant lion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קיסר assumed the פסוק meant an ordinary lion that a horseman can kill.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק means the lion of בי עילאי, which no person can overcome.

steps.title: The emperor insists on seeing the lion, and it is brought
steps.stepSummary: The קיסר asks to see the lion. רבי יהושע בן חנניה warns him he cannot, but the קיסר insists. רבי יהושע prays, and the lion leaves its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The emperor said: I want you to show it to me. He answered: You cannot see it. The emperor said: Truly, I will see it! רבי יהושע prayed for mercy, and the lion was uprooted from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. The קיסר demands to see the lion despite a warning, so רבי יהושע prays and the lion sets out toward Rome.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning "you cannot see it" is important, because the next step shows what happens when the lion even comes near. The קיסר's insistence sets up the lesson that he is overreaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It was uprooted from its place, it set off

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בָּעֵינָא דְּמַיחֲזֵית לֵיהּ נִיהֲלִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: I want you to show it to me.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא מָצֵית חָזֵית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: You cannot see it.
He said to him: Truly, I will see it!
He prayed for mercy,
and it was uprooted from its place,
phrases.notes: "It" is the lion of בי עילאי, which now starts heading toward Rome.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The קיסר responds to the answer by asking for proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Despite the warning, the קיסר insists, and through prayer the lion is brought out.

steps.title: The lion's roars devastate Rome from far away
steps.stepSummary: From four hundred פרסאות away, one roar makes pregnant women miscarry and knocks down Rome's wall. From three hundred פרסאות away, another roar makes men's teeth fall out and throws the קיסר off his throne.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it was four hundred פרסאות away, it roared once, and all the pregnant women miscarried, and the wall of Rome fell. When it was three hundred פרסאות away, it roared again, and the men's back and front teeth fell out, and the emperor himself fell from his throne to the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes what the lion's roar did, even from very far away. Each roar gets closer and worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proves רבי יהושע's point: no horseman could face this lion, since just hearing it from hundreds of פרסאות away is too much. It also explains the warning "you cannot see it", because the קיסר could not even handle hearing it.

keyTerms.meaning: פרסאות, a large measure of distance (parasangs)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה מְרַחַיק אַרְבַּע מְאָה פַּרְסֵי,
phrases.english: When it was four hundred parasangs away,
it roared one roar,
all the pregnant women miscarried,
and the wall of Rome fell.
When it was three hundred parasangs away,
it roared another roar,
the back teeth and front teeth of the men fell out,
and he too fell from the throne to the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה מְרַחַיק אַרְבַּע מְאָה פַּרְסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what happened as the lion approached.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read אפילו as "even" here. In this line it means the women miscarried.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lion's roar alone, from hundreds of פרסאות away, brought down Rome's wall and the קיסר himself.

steps.title: The emperor begs, and the lion is sent back
steps.stepSummary: The terrified קיסר begs רבי יהושע to pray for the lion to go back. He prays, and it returns to its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The emperor said to him: I beg you, pray for mercy that it go back to its place. He prayed for mercy, and it returned to its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The first story ends. The קיסר gives in and begs for the lion to be sent away, and רבי יהושע's prayer sends it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man who mocked the comparison now admits its power by begging. The story's point is settled: God is compared to a lion no human can face, so the comparison does show His greatness.
steps.whatToRemember: The קיסר said a lion is weak because a horseman can kill one. רבי יהושע בן חנניה showed that God is compared to the lion of בי עילאי, whose roar alone, from hundreds of פרסאות away, overwhelmed Rome.

phrases.english: He said to him: I beg you,
pray for mercy about it, that it should go back to its place.
He prayed for mercy about it,
and it went back to its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The קיסר reacts to the devastation, and the story closes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The comparison of God to a lion shows real greatness, because it refers to a lion no human can withstand.

steps.title: A new story: the emperor asks to see God
steps.stepSummary: A second story begins. The קיסר asks to see God Himself, רבי יהושע says he cannot, and the קיסר starts to insist. The story continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The emperor said to רבי יהושע בן חנניה: I want to see your God. He said: You cannot see Him. The emperor said: Truly...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story with the same two people. This step only sets things up; the answer comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats the first story: request, warning, insistence. Having just seen that the קיסר could not handle a lion, the learner can expect that seeing God will be even more impossible.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ קֵיסָר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה:
phrases.english: The emperor said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya:
I want to see your God.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא מָצֵית חָזֵית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: You cannot see Him.
He said to him: Truly...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the lion story ends, a parallel story about seeing God begins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The קיסר wants to see the God of the Jews with his own eyes.
